# Hypergate

> Connect everything once, for all. Hypergate is a local-first gateway where you connect your MCP servers, connectors, agents, and skills one time, and you, your team, and every agent you run (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Nekko Agent) get all of it the moment you connect. Setup is one click, permissions are set per human or per agent (a model or company you trust less can get a narrower set), and every access lands in a local audit log. Under the hood it runs your MCP servers on your own machine, sandboxed and supervised, behind **one gateway endpoint**, so the authentication, keys, and permissions for services like GitHub, Vercel, Slack, or Google Drive are **not** in the agent's hands. Open source, MIT, by Nekko Labs.

Hypergate is not a connector directory: it is a proper server runtime. Add servers from a curated catalog or a custom command, choose how each one is isolated, start them, and paste a single URL (or stdio command) into your agent. Every tool call is recorded locally, so you get an audit trail and usage analytics for free, and secrets are injected rather than logged.

## Key facts

- **What it is**: a supervisor plus an aggregating MCP gateway that runs on localhost. Agent harnesses are MCP *clients*; Hypergate is the *server* side they need.
- **One endpoint for every agent**: the gateway merges every ready server's tools (namespaced `server__tool`) into one MCP server, exposed over streamable HTTP at `/mcp` with bearer-token auth, and over stdio via `hypergated --stdio` (which attaches to a running daemon rather than starting a second copy of every server).
- **Connecting a client**: the manager wires up Claude Code, the Gemini CLI, Cursor, VS Code, Nekko Agent and `.mcp.json` in one click, each with its own scoped token. Claude Code also has a plugin (`claude plugin marketplace add nekko-labs/hypergate`, then `claude plugin install hypergate@nekko-labs`) and Claude Desktop an `.mcpb` extension; both fetch a credential at connect time via `hypergate mcp-headers`, so nothing breaks when a token rotates. Hypergate cannot be added as a claude.ai *custom connector*: those are opened from Anthropic's cloud and must be public `https://` servers, which a local gateway is not.
- **Isolation is a choice per server**: **Process sandbox** (the default, no dependencies: scrubbed and allow-listed env, injected secrets only, restricted CWD and limits, no shell), **Docker** (container per server, dropped caps, no-new-privileges), or **Remote** (an authenticated HTTP client to a provider's hosted MCP endpoint, nothing runs locally).
- **Catalog**: curated first-party servers with verified launch configs (Nekko Agent, Context7, Supabase, Linear, Figma, GitHub, Atlassian, AWS, Azure, GCP, Cloudflare, Fly.io, and more), Official/Community trust chips, one-click OAuth for remote first-party servers, plus search over the official MCP registry at `registry.modelcontextprotocol.io`.
- **Observability**: durable usage history and logs (SQLite), a tool inspector showing each tool's description and typed parameters parsed from the live schema, and a command-line-tools radar that detects which CLIs your servers depend on (node/npx, uv/uvx, docker, flyctl, cloud CLIs) with version, path, and an install hint when missing.
- **Local-first and private**: everything runs on your machine under `~/.hypergate`. No account, no cloud dependency.
- **Licence**: MIT, open source.

## Install

- **Installers** (nothing else required, not even Node): `-setup.exe` for Windows, `.dmg` for macOS, `.deb`/`.rpm`/tarball for Linux, x64 and arm64, from the [latest release](https://github.com/nekko-labs/hypergate/releases). Open the macOS disk image and drag Hypergate.app to Applications; no admin prompt.
- **npm** (Node 20+, 22.5+ recommended for durable analytics): `npm install -g hypergated`, then `hypergate start`. Two lines, and the second one is the whole setup: it starts the daemon, creates a launcher, and opens the manager. `--no-open`/`--no-shortcut` turn either half off, and both are skipped automatically on CI, over SSH, and on a Linux box with no display. `npx hypergated` runs it without installing.
- **Two commands**: `hypergate` (CLI and tray agent) and `hypergated` (the daemon alone, for headless boxes, WSL, and containers). The npm package is named `hypergated` because `hypergate` on npm belongs to an unrelated project; the command you type is still `hypergate`.
- **Updating**: `hypergate update` reports what is installed and what is available; `hypergate update --apply` installs it and restarts Hypergate (npm installs; other channels are given the exact command). `hypergate status` and the manager's topbar surface it too.

## Architecture (brief)

- `packages/shared`: types and the daemon API contract.
- `packages/core`: the RuntimeAdapter (Process | Docker | Remote), the Supervisor, the aggregating Gateway, and the registry client.
- `apps/daemon`: `hypergated`, one localhost port serving the web UI, the management API, and the streamable-HTTP MCP gateway at `/mcp`.
- `apps/web`: the management UI, served by the daemon.
- `apps/shell`: the Rust tray agent and CLI.
- `apps/site`: this marketing page.
